PERFORMANCE (P)=persistent. Each description names the lightest choice for performance:

FAST checks every 0.02 s and catches the shortest spikes, but is the heaviest. BALANCED checks every 0.05 s. LIGHT checks every 0.1 s and is the lightest for performance: a very brief acceleration spike can be missed, while an impact below 100 ft is still caught by the speed it removes and by the touchdown speed.

ON is the lightest for performance: the impact monitor sleeps above 450 ft above ground and wakes below 400 ft or on the ground. OFF keeps it always active (heaviest) and also covers a crash against a cliff or an obstacle higher than that.

BASIC is the lightest for performance: slower diagnostic sampling and only the essential events, while the snapshots needed for a bug report are kept. ADVANCED records every diagnostic detail and is the heaviest.

FIRST START: IMPORTANT INFO BELOW! PLEASE READ TO THE END!
Welcome to the HEMS dispatch system.
You're going to receive a dispatch from your HEMS company instructing you about the assigned mission. Missions are designed as follow:

You will starts from any location you like which will be set as your home base. Upon dispatch acceptance, proceed to the accident site where you can either land for a ground rescue or perform a hoist operation while remaining in flight.
Patient may be (or may not) carried by the helicopter. In case you have to reach an hospital, select the hospital destination where the patient will be transported.
After the patient unloading, you may end the mission or return to home base. Home base may be the starting point or any other point on the map.
During return trip, you may receive a new dispatch and decide if ignore it or accept a new mission.

The system needs external packages to spawn various objects filling the accident site scenes. Rescue vehicles are dynamically spawn and interact with the user when present. Mission may automatically select national rescue vehicles provided the relative addon package is installed.
The following addons are used by the mission. Some are optional, some are mandatory. NOTE: INSTALL PACKAGES IN THE GIVEN ORDER (YOU MAY SKIP OPTIONALS YOU DON'T WANT)
NOTE: Although these packages are independent, you must install the 68PonyGT National packages before the '68PonyGT Action pack HEMS Objects' pack.

If you encounter mission lock issues, simply reinstall the '68PonyGT Action pack HEMS Objects' pack and allow it to overwrite existing files. This ensures that newer versions of shared objects replace older ones, preventing potential conflicts. For more info:

VOICEPACKS: Different voicepacks are available to improve the experience! Download them and switch to them in the SETTINGS/AUDIO OPTIONS page. Here below you find links for not already installed or outdated voicepacks.

At startup, the briefing page will be proposed. A red message may ask you to connect the radio installed on the interseat console. The radio must be switched on, and, when requested, the 'PICK' button has to be pushed. Radio will remain connected until helicopter or radio power off.

Once connected, either wait for a dispatch (it will appear after a random delay), or push NEXT DISPATCH to immediately receive a dispatch. Location of the proposed dispatch may be reviewed on the map. Push ACCEPT DISPATCH to begin the mission.

hide briefing = Hide the briefing page of the tablet

repeat dispatch = The dispatcher reads the dispatch again
read briefing = The copilot or the doctor reads the briefing
next dispatch = Ask for the next dispatch
request ambulance = Request an ambulance (the dispatcher accepts)

time to destination = Time to the destination of the phase

skid landing = Land on the skids at the scene

ground operations = Stay here and continue with ground operations

patient status = Patient status: the doctor in flight, the ground team on the polycon during ground operations
